Control of Congress headlined a historic 2026 midterm election. Democrats took power in the House and Senate, tallying victory after victory to repaint the electoral map in broad swaths of blue. Those victories included triumphs in the Senate and governor races in Iowa where water pollution from industrial agriculture and the state’s rising cancer rate were prominent campaign issues . Down the ballot, voters in state and local elections were asked to approve new spending on water infrastructure or changes in water policy. Voters, as they typically do, supported public funding for water infrastructure. Sign up In Arkansas , voters endorsed a measure to authorize the state Natural Resources Commission to issue $500 million in general obligation bonds to finance water and wastewater systems, pollution reduction, flood control, and irrigation. The measure passed with 56 percent support after being put on the ballot by the Republican-controlled Legislature. In Louisiana , voters approved an amendment to the state Constitution that will allow public funds to be spent on removing the part of a lead service line that rests on private property. Advocates say that the change will unlock federal funding for lead pipe replacement and speed the process of eliminating lead from drinking water in homes and businesses.
